introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. 0562 Citizenship Education 2, Subject Title: Citizenship Education, Paper 2, Subject Code 0562, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2023. Duration: Two and a half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- You are required to answer FOUR questions choosing QUESTION 1 and THREE others from Sections A, B and C.
- All the questions carry equal marks and marks allocated to different parts of questions are indicated.
- Extra question(s) answered from each section shall NOT be marked.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Question 1 (COMPULSORY)**

Study this extract bearing on the inaugural speech by the Head of State on the occasion of the swearing-in ceremony in 2011 and then answer questions (a) to (d) that follow. (The maximum marks for each sub-question is indicated in brackets).

> "... In this temple of democracy, I also wish to once again thank all Cameroonians for having renewed their trust in me. It goes without saying that such trust will be an invaluable moral support to me in the discharge of the heavy responsibilities awaiting me in the coming years... It is an expression of absolute loyalty to the institutions of the Republic and the personal commitment to perform the duties of Head of State as set forth in our Constitution.
> Over time, our democratic system has been gradually taking root, consolidating and improving ... The National Assembly will soon be backed by a Senate...
>
> On the whole, I think we have reasons to be satisfied with the progress made in our democratic process. Measures have been taken to guarantee the regularity and transparency of elections... In two decades, a lot has been done to hold free, fair and transparent elections. Although progress has definitely been made in electoral democracy, it remains that some adjustments have to be made to our electoral body to improve its functioning.
> However, I must say that individual behaviours are not always consistent with the solidarity which is supposed to be the hallmark of a democratic society. More often than not, self-interest takes precedence over general interest. Such a mindset is the cause of social ills such as fraud, corruption and even delinquency...
>
> Long live the Republic, Long live Cameroon."

*Source: Cameroon Radio Television, Yaounde, 3rd November 2011*

**QUESTIONS**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Identify by name the Head of State who made the speech.

(ii) What arm of government is headed by the President of the Republic named in (a) (i) above?

(iii) Name **TWO** duties of the Head of State as set forth in the Cameroon Constitution.

**[1+1+2 marks]**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The speech was made by **Paul Biya**, President of the Republic of Cameroon. The extract does not give the name, but the source line (CRTV, 3rd November 2011) shows that it is the speech made when the President was sworn in after the 2011 presidential election.

**(ii)** The President of the Republic heads the **Executive** (the arm of government that carries out and enforces the laws and runs the administration of the country).

**(iii)** Any **two** of the duties of the Head of State set out in the Constitution:

- He **represents the State** and is the Head of State.
- He **ensures respect for the Constitution** and the regular functioning of public institutions.
- He is the **guarantor of the independence of the nation, of its territorial integrity and of the continuity of the State**, and of respect for treaties and international agreements.
- He **appoints the Prime Minister and the members of Government** and appoints to senior civil and military posts.
- He **promulgates (signs into law) the laws** passed by Parliament.
- He accredits Cameroonian ambassadors abroad and receives foreign ambassadors.
- He exercises the **right of pardon**.
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Which legal institution in Cameroon is the President referring to as the "temple of democracy", in line 1 of the extract?

(ii) In which year was the promise made in **line 7** of the extract fulfilled?

(iii) State **TWO** conditions to be fulfilled by a Cameroonian vying for the post of a Senator.

**[1+1+2 marks]**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The "temple of democracy" is **Parliament, the National Assembly**: the institution where the representatives of the people make the laws, and the place where the swearing-in ceremony took place.

**(ii)** Line 7 contains the promise that "the National Assembly will soon be backed by a Senate". It was fulfilled in **2013**, when the first senatorial elections were held and the Senate was set up as the second chamber of Parliament.

**(iii)** Any **two** conditions (as laid down by the Constitution and the Electoral Code):

- The candidate must be a **Cameroonian citizen**.
- He or she must reach the **minimum age fixed by law** for a senator.
- He or she must **enjoy civil and political rights** (must not be disqualified by a court judgement).
- The candidate must be **presented by a political party** and meet the formal requirements of the electoral law (for example, a deposit and a complete file).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Apart from Presidential and Senatorial elections, state **TWO** other types of elections carried out in Cameroon.

(ii) Identify **TWO** weaknesses of the Cameroon electoral process.

(iii) What **TWO** measures have been taken by the Cameroon Government to improve on the country's electoral process?

**[2+2+2 marks]**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Any **two** of:

- **Legislative (parliamentary) elections**, to elect the Members of Parliament of the National Assembly.
- **Municipal (council) elections**, to elect municipal councillors.
- **Regional elections**, to elect regional councillors (first held in December 2020).

**(ii)** Any **two** weaknesses:

- **Electoral fraud and irregularities** (multiple voting, vote buying, tampered results) reported by some parties and observers.
- **Voter apathy**: many citizens, especially young people, do not register or do not vote because they doubt that their vote counts.
- **Problems with voters' registers and cards**: names missing or wrongly spelt, late distribution of voters' cards.
- **Doubts about the independence of the electoral body** and weak access of opposition parties to resources and the media.

**(iii)** Any **two** measures:

- The creation of an **electoral body, Elections Cameroon (ELECAM)**, to organise and supervise elections.
- The adoption of a **single Electoral Code** (2012) bringing together the rules governing elections.
- The introduction of **biometric voter registration** to reduce multiple registration and impersonation.
- The creation of the **Constitutional Council**, which handles electoral disputes and proclaims results of national elections.
- The accreditation of **election observers** and of the **representatives of parties** in polling stations, to improve transparency.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Define social ills as mentioned in the passage.

(ii) What are the consequences of the social ills mentioned in **line 15** above?

(iii) Outline measures that have been put in place by the government of Cameroon to fight against corruption in the country.

**[1+3+2 marks]**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **Social ills** are harmful or immoral behaviours and practices (such as fraud, corruption and delinquency) that damage the well-being and the moral values of individuals and of the whole society.

**(ii)** Fraud, corruption and delinquency have many consequences. Any three, explained:

- **Loss of public money and slower development**: funds meant for schools, roads and hospitals are diverted, so projects are poorly done or abandoned.
- **Injustice and inequality**: those who bribe or cheat gain advantages over honest citizens.
- **Loss of trust in institutions**: citizens stop believing in the administration, the courts or elections.
- **Insecurity and crime**: delinquency leads to theft, violence, drug abuse and a climate of fear.
- **Bad image of the country**, which scares off investors and reduces foreign aid.
- **Moral decay**: honesty, hard work and solidarity are replaced by self-interest.

**(iii)** Any **two** measures (outlined):

- The creation of the **National Anti-Corruption Commission (CONAC)** in 2006, to receive complaints, investigate and prevent corruption.
- The creation of the **National Agency for Financial Investigation (ANIF)** to track suspicious financial operations.
- The creation of the **Special Criminal Court** (2011) to try cases of embezzlement of public funds, and the prosecution and imprisonment of persons found guilty.
- The **declaration of assets** by senior officials, provided for in the Constitution, and audits by control bodies such as the Supreme State Audit and the Audit Bench of the Supreme Court.
- **Sensitisation campaigns** and **anti-corruption cells** in public services, and the rules on public contracts (tenders) to make them transparent.
